hypothesis_update: Working hypothesis: component-local init statements are rewritten with an empty alias/scope set (`&HashSet::new()`), and if that parameter controls name resolution, a component's init will fail to resolve (or silently leave unrewritten) references to its own state or to sibling components, while the compose-level init (given the full `&components` map) resolves correctly — i.e., an asymmetric resolution bug that would surface as dangling `alias__field`/qualified names or spurious CoreError in the lowered kernel. Secondary lower-confidence lead: the final `SpecItem::Init` is appended after all static `State`/other items (line 360) before actions are extended, so init may not precede dependent items in the composed kernel.
rationale: The target body shows two init paths that resolve names differently: each component's own init is rewritten via `rewrite_statements(statements.clone(), component, &HashSet::new())` (line 315-319) with an empty third argument, while the compose-level init is rewritten via `rewrite_compose_statements(statements.clone(), &components)` (line 345) with the full component map. The `statement-rewrite` card holds the definitions of both functions, so it directly reveals what the empty `HashSet` parameter gates (e.g. in-scope aliases, binder scope, or a visited/visited-name set) and whether a component-local init can resolve its own or sibling names at all. This is the sharpest concrete anomaly in the evidence and a single card that resolves it.
